newsitem.title: UK: Consumer cos see households driving online sales.
newsitem.headline: Consumer cos see households driving online sales.

text.p: More than 50 percent of the world's leading companies selling fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) have a presence on the Internet, and the vast majority believe households will drive on-line sales, a market research group reported on Tuesday.

But despite the positive outlook for selling consumer goods via the Internet, traditional media will continue to play a key role in attracting consumers to World Wide Web sites, London-based Datamonitor said.
The market research group said respondents to its survey, FMCG on the Internet: From Branding to Sales, estimated that 80-90 percent of online sales would derive from households in the year 2001.

In some cases, online sales are expected to account for a significant proportion of total product sales. Respondents estimated that five to 10 percent of spirits sales would be generated from the World Wide Web, with retailers expected to have a one to two percent edge over manufacturers, Datamonitor said.

Two-thirds of respondents believe it will be most important to advertise Web sites via traditional media up to 2001. Search-engine advertising was named as the second most desirable advertising vehicle, followed by on-line advertising, Datamonitor said.

"This indicates a perception among FMCG executives that the Web cannot function as a stand-alone advertising medium and, even in five years' time, will still rely on traditional media for support," Datamonitor said.
